claim: HIV-1 transcriptionally active cells are detectable in perinatally infected infants at 1-2 months by scRNA-seq, at 1 in ~1,128 CD4 T cells, and reside in CD4 subsets including a regulatory T cell
novelty: GENUINE GAP. Naive CD4 as a proviral DNA reservoir is published in children 5-11y (JCI 2025) and infant macaques (2021), and RNA+ DGE is published in adults (eLife 2025) — but transcriptionally ACTIVE infected cells profiled by scRNA-seq in human infants at 1-2 months pre-ART have not been shown
risk: LOW. Descriptive, controlled, and the detection ceiling is stated
verdict: DO THIS. It is the defensible version of Lesley's point and needs no new compute

claim: Infected cells in infants are found in the NAIVE CD4 compartment, contrary to the adult memory-reservoir dogma
novelty: Would be striking IF supported. But our own data does not support it: of 4 cells, one is a Treg on positive FOXP3/IL2RA/IKZF2 evidence, one is discrepant between its published effector-memory label and its naive module score, one is too shallow to call, and only one leans naive with low confidence
effort: Realign 5-15 samples (1-5 weeks) AND still likely underpowered
risk: HIGH. PLOS Pathogens 2026 explicitly flags memory-cell contamination of naive gates as the central weakness of this exact claim. With n=4 and one Treg among them, a reviewer would reject it
verdict: DO NOT CLAIM. State the subset distribution descriptively and name it as the hypothesis the data raises but cannot settle

option: 3. DGE: RNA+ vs RNA- CD4 at entry
claim: Infected CD4 cells differ transcriptionally from uninfected CD4 in the same infant
novelty: Method has direct precedent (eLife 2025, 985 RNA+ cells in adults). Not novel as a design; novel only in infants
cells_needed: Hundreds. eLife had 985. We would have 4 now, ~13 at 5 samples, ~47 at 15
risk: VERY HIGH. 4 vs 2,705 cells gives no usable statistics — any DEG list would be driven by single cells and depth. Presenting it invites a methods rejection
verdict: NOT with these numbers. If pursued, needs targeted enrichment, not more realignment

option: 4. Targeted hypothesis: restriction factors / IFN genes in RNA+ cells
claim: RNA+ cells show reduced interferon-stimulated gene and restriction-factor expression, consistent with the permissive-cell signature
novelty: Directly tests the published permissiveness signature (PMC5658171) in infants, and connects to THIS PAPER'S OWN type I IFN thread in Figures 4-5
cells_needed: 4 as a descriptive observation; 20+ for a statistic
risk: MODERATE as descriptive. Must be framed as an observation in 4 cells, not a test
verdict: WORTH COMPUTING NOW. It is the one analysis that ties the HIV+ cells to the paper's existing interferon story rather than sitting as an orphan result

option: 5. Report as a resource / methods contribution
claim: A combined GRCh38+HIV-1 reference and control framework (ambient, lineage, dose-response) for detecting vRNA+ cells in infant CITE-seq data
novelty: Modest, but the three-control framework is more rigorous than a raw count and is reusable
verdict: INCLUDE as a supplementary methods note supporting option 1
